changes.before: Input comes from outside the program. java.util.Scanner is a library class that reads tokens, pieces separated by whitespace by default.
changes.after: Check whether input is a whole number before reading it as an int.

before: Input comes from outside the program. java.util.Scanner is a library class that reads tokens, pieces separated by whitespace by default.
new java.util.Scanner(System.in) creates a reader for standard input. Scanner is the type and input is the variable name. Using the full class name avoids an import line here.
input.hasNextInt() checks whether the next token can be read as an int; it does not consume the token. It can wait while input is unavailable.
When that check is true, input.nextInt() consumes the token and returns its integer value. The else block handles an unsuitable token or exhausted input without attempting that conversion.
This is one token, not an entire form. Real applications also decide allowed ranges and how to retry. Here a successful number is simply echoed.
after: Input is information that comes from outside the program. Scanner reads pieces called tokens. By default, spaces and other whitespace separate those pieces.

new java.util.Scanner(System.in) creates a reader for standard input, usually the terminal. input names that reader. The full name java.util.Scanner identifies the library class without an import line.
hasNextInt() checks whether the next token can be read as an int within its range. It leaves that token in the input. The check may wait for input to arrive or end.
When the check succeeds, nextInt() consumes that token and returns its integer value. Otherwise, the else branch shows guidance without attempting the integer read.
Being readable as an integer does not prove a number is allowed for your task. Range rules and retry behavior need their own code. This example reads one token and prints an accepted integer.

before.question: With the single token hello, what does this program do?
choices: Prints the guidance message without calling nextInt.
before.explanation: hasNextInt is false for hello, so the guarded numeric read is skipped.

after.question: If the next token is hello, what does this program do?
choices: Print the guidance message without calling nextInt().
Print hello as if it were an integer.
after.explanation: hello is not an int token. The false check selects the else branch and skips nextInt().
